setup_summary.text: JPM reports fiscal Q4 2026 on 2027-01-14 after the close. Consensus is EPS $5.92 and revenue $51.79B.

Q3 2026 results from the call: net income $15.3B, EPS $5.57, ROTCE 20%, revenue $50.9B (management says up 8% year on year) and expenses $27.3B (up 12%). Results included $658M of net investment securities losses in Corporate. EPS was up about 10% on the $5.07 of Q3 2025.

Use the right base for Q4 growth. Q4 2025 revenue was $45.80B and diluted EPS $4.63, and that quarter carried a $2.2B Apple Card provision. Consensus therefore implies about +13.1% revenue and +27.9% EPS year on year. The fact-sheet derived growth rates (+11.5% revenue, +16.8% EPS) divide by the Q3 2025 quarter and should not be used.
A second consensus (Zacks, 2026-10-30) has Q4 EPS at $5.96 (+14% year on year) and FY26 EPS at $24.97 (+22.8%). FY27 EPS is $25.87, only +3.6%, and the 30-day revision was -0.9%.

Earnings track record: 3 beats and 1 miss in the last 4 quarters, average surprise +2.2%. The average closing move over the last 8 reports is about 2.1%. No whisper number or options-implied move is available yet.

Street positioning is steady. All seven rating actions in the last 30 days were 'maintained' (Citigroup Neutral, Truist Hold, Baird Neutral, Morgan Stanley Equal Weight, RBC Outperform, Barclays Overweight, UBS Buy). Consensus price target is $373.36, 10.8% above $337.04.
The Q2 2026 baseline was inflated by one-offs. Net income was $21.2B (+41%) and EPS $7.70, including a $4.6B Visa gain and $1.0B of equity-investment gains. H1 net income was $37.65B (+27.1%).

Capital is being held back rather than returned. Standardized CET1 was 13.9% at Q3, down 30bp from 14.2% at Q2. An analyst put the Q3 buyback at about $1B against a roughly $7B norm, and Q2 repurchases were $6.7B. Dimon says the firm has roughly $30B of excess capital.

last_reported.text: Q3 2026 EPS was $5.57, after $658M of pre-tax net investment securities losses.

view.text: Consensus asks for about +6% sequentially. The securities losses were worth roughly $0.19 a share after tax at a ~23% rate (my arithmetic, with Q2's 23.1% tax rate as the proxy). A repeat of the 2.2% average beat would put EPS near $6.05.

Consensus sits about 1.7% above Q3 even though management's base case is a normal seasonal Markets decline. With total NII guided to about $28B, consensus implies about $23.8B of noninterest revenue if the NII guide is on the same basis as reported revenue (unconfirmed). The risk to the revenue number is Markets and IB fees, not NII.

last_reported.text: Q2 2026 NII ex-Markets was $23.68B. The Q3 figure is not in the sources.

view.text: Guidance of about $25.5B looks above the July path. The $96.5B full-year guide less H1's $46.96B left about $49.5B, or roughly $24.8B a quarter, for H2 (derived). Hitting $25.5B would confirm NII upside and underpins the $107B 2027 case.

last_reported.text: Q2 2026 reported NII was $25.51B, of which Markets NII was $1.945B.

view.text: The $28B guide less $25.5B ex-Markets implies about $2.5B of Markets NII, against $1.9B in Q2. Markets NII is offset in principal transactions, so judge Markets on total revenue.

last_reported.text: Q3 2026 expenses were $27.3B, up 12% year on year.

view.text: Q4 is guided to about $27.5B, only $0.2B above Q3. The guide is on an adjusted basis (ex-legal), and management ties the increase to volume- and revenue-related expense. A stronger Markets or IB quarter would push comp higher. Consensus for 2027 expense is about $114B, and management's preliminary read is not far from it.

last_reported.text: Q2 2026 Markets revenue was $12.08B (+35%). In Q3, equities were up 49% and fixed income down 4% year on year (dollar figures not in the sources).

view.text: There is no consensus in the sources. Barnum's base case is a normal seasonal decline from Q3 to Q4. Dimon expects 'not the same seasonal decline' because of events in the world. That split is the main swing factor versus the $51.79B revenue consensus.

last_reported.text: Q3 IB fees were up 14% year on year, strong across products and notably in advisory. Q2 firmwide IB fees were $3.21B.

view.text: Management says evolving market conditions 'have recently slowed activity a bit', and the slowdown showed in the second half of September after the rate sell-off. The pipeline is 'like an accordion'. Watch for a sequential step-down in fees.

last_reported.text: Q2 2026 Card Services NCO rate was 3.34% (H1: 3.40%).

view.text: The ~3.2% full-year guide with H1 at 3.40% implies H2 near 3.0% on a simple average (my arithmetic), well below Q2. Card 30+ delinquencies were 1.91% and 90+ were 1.00% at Q2. The call reiterated the guide, so there is little room for a miss.

last_reported.text: Q3 credit costs were $2.7B, with net charge-offs of $2.2B and a net reserve build of $539M.

view.text: The wholesale build came from new activity, not downgrades or a worse outlook. With rates rising and unemployment risk elevated, Q4 depends on loan growth and any change in macro weights. The allowance already puts extra weight on adverse scenarios.

last_reported.text: The ratio was 13.9% at Q3, down 30bp, as net income was more than offset by OCI losses, higher RWA and distributions.

view.text: The requirement is 11.5%. Management is choosing to keep dry powder for organic deployment, and RWA rose about $52B in Q3. Higher rates add OCI risk, and the Basel III and GSIB finalizations are expected around year end (per an analyst).

since_filing.text: The Q3 print (after the August 10-Q) showed net income of $15.3B and EPS of $5.57. Revenue was up 8% and expenses up 12%. CCB revenue was +9%, CIB revenue +14% and AWM revenue +14%. AUM was $5.2T and client assets $7.9T.

The 10-Q's July outlook gave full-year NII of about $105.5B, NII ex-Markets of about $96.5B and adjusted expense of about $107.5B. The call replaced these with Q4 targets (NII $28B, ex-Markets $25.5B, expense $27.5B) plus a 2027 central case. The full-year figures on the call's guidance page are not in the transcript.
On Oct 20, 2026 JPM closed $7.0B of Parent Company notes: $350M floating due 2030, $2.9B fixed-to-floating due 2030 and $3.75B fixed-to-floating due 2037.

The 10-Q disclosed a new $50B buyback authorization effective July 1 and an intended Q3 dividend of $1.65, up from $1.50. Actual Q3 repurchases appear to have fallen sharply, with an analyst citing about $1B.

WSJ (2026-10-19) reports JPM has financed $230B of projects through its $1.5T Security and Resiliency Initiative in year one. Dimon cited more than $200B on the call and said the capital can be redeployed at better returns than buybacks.
CNBC (2026-10-21) says Goldman, JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley booked a combined $52B of stock trading revenue year to date, nearly 80% of the total. This is consistent with JPM equities up 49% in Q3.

A conflict to note between dates: the 10-Q (Aug) put the allowance on a central case of 4.1-4.2% unemployment. The Q3 call (newer) flags rising rates with 10-year yields possibly near 6% and Fed hikes in the forward curve. This is a new macro backdrop since the filing.

key_debates.question: Can NII deliver the $107B 2027 central case in a rising-rate regime?

bull.text: The firm remains asset-sensitive, with lower-than-modeled deposit betas. Net new checking accounts were about 650,000 in Q3 and consumer deposits grew 4%. About half of the $5B step-up comes from the curve and forward hikes, and the rest from balance-sheet growth and mix.

bear.text: The rate cycle is unprecedented from this launch point, so historical beta data is thin. Higher rates could drive migration out of checking and savings into CDs and premium products, adding deposit pressure. Management itself says the 2027 case is highly uncertain.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 NII ex-Markets versus the $25.5B guide, plus the refined 2027 guide on the Q4 call.

key_debates.question: Is the low buyback pace smart capital stewardship or an EPS headwind?

bull.text: About $30B of excess capital remains, and organic deployment (Security and Resiliency, American Dream and Commercial Banking initiatives) is expected to earn better returns than buying stock at a roughly 6% earnings yield. Standardized CET1 of 13.9% sits well above the 11.5% requirement.

bear.text: Repurchases fell from $6.7B in Q2 to about $1B in Q3, removing a tailwind to per-share growth. The March 2026 Basel III re-proposal would raise required CET1 by about 6% (about 4% combined with the GSIB proposal), so the cushion is not as large as it looks.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 repurchase amount, CET1 ratio and any final Basel III/GSIB outcome around year end.

key_debates.question: Can Markets and IB revenue carry a Q4 revenue consensus above Q3?

bull.text: Equities were up 49% in Q3 and the three big banks hold nearly 80% of stock trading revenue. The IB pipeline is healthy, including European IPOs, and Dimon says there will not be the usual seasonal decline.

bear.text: Barnum's base case is a normal seasonal decline. IB activity slowed in late September after the rate sell-off, and fixed income was down 4% in Q3. Consensus revenue of $51.79B is already 1.7% above Q3.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 Markets revenue and IB fees against the seasonal base case.

key_debates.question: Does consumer and corporate credit hold as rates rise?

bull.text: The consumer is very healthy on a strong labor market, and the wholesale reserve build came from new activity rather than downgrades. Corporate balance sheets are in quite good shape.

bear.text: A long, aggressive rate cycle would raise unemployment and weaken consumer credit. Management is already tightening credit terms because of loose covenants and priming. The card NCO guide implies H2 near 3.0% versus 3.34% in Q2.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 net charge-offs, Card NCO versus the 3.2% guide, and the size of the reserve build.

description.text: EPS lands in a $5.9-6.05 range (illustrative), in line to a modest beat. NII and expense hit guidance (about $28B and $27.5B), Markets declines seasonally and the 2027 NII case is reaffirmed around $107B.

scenarios.name: bear

description.text: EPS falls short of the $5.92 consensus, below about $5.75 (illustrative). IB activity stalls after the rate shock, Markets drops sharply, expense runs above $27.5B on revenue-related items, or a larger reserve build occurs.

triggers: IB fees step down materially on valuation gaps
Fixed income weakness persists alongside normal equities seasonality
Higher unemployment risk or downgrades lead to a larger reserve build
Deposit migration pressures the 2027 NII outlook or net securities losses recur

claim.text: Rising rates and a bond sell-off, including a possible 6% 10-year and Fed hikes, could hurt the NII path through deposit migration and higher paid rates. They could also slow client activity and add OCI and capital pressure (CET1 fell 30bp in Q3 partly on OCI losses).
Q4 Markets and IB revenue is exposed to seasonality and event risk. IB activity paused after the rate sell-off, and Barnum and Dimon disagree on the size of the seasonal decline.

Consumer and corporate credit could weaken if elevated real rates persist. Loose covenants, priming and hedge-fund and leveraged-finance leverage are watch areas. The card NCO guide of ~3.2% depends on a sharp H2 improvement.

Concentration risk is building around AI and hyperscaler financing. Exposures are 'quite modest' today, but the AI theme is diffused across construction lending, working-capital revolvers and equities.

Capital rules are shifting. The March 2026 Basel III re-proposal would raise required CET1 by about 6%, or about 4% together with the GSIB proposal. The GSIB surcharge would fall to 5.2% from 5.5% under that proposal. Finalization is expected around year end per an analyst.

Expense growth is running ahead (Q3 +12% year on year, Q4 guide about $27.5B) on volume and revenue-related costs, front-office hiring and wage inflation. 2027 consensus is about $114B, with AI and token costs as an added uncertainty.

Agentic AI and fintech competition for yield-seeking deposits and for the customer relationship. Management says it is not complacent, blocks credential-sharing agents and focuses on primary-bank relationships.

questions_for_management.question: How much of the $5B step-up from the Q4 annualized $102B to $107B of 2027 NII ex-Markets relies on forward-curve hikes, and how does it change if consumer deposit betas or migration surprise?

why.text: The 2027 central case is the biggest new datapoint, and management says it is highly uncertain.

questions_for_management.question: What is the Q4 buyback level and the capital target? When do repurchases resume at the old pace, and how does the Basel III and GSIB outcome change that?

why.text: Q3 repurchases fell sharply to about $1B from $6.7B in Q2 while CET1 slipped to 13.9%.

questions_for_management.question: How are Q4 Markets and IB tracking quarter to date versus a normal seasonal decline, and what is behind Dimon's view that the decline will not be the same?

why.text: Barnum and Dimon gave different seasonal reads, and consensus revenue is above Q3.

questions_for_management.question: What is the new full-year adjusted expense figure and the preliminary 2027 outlook, including AI and token costs and front-office hiring?

why.text: Q4 expense guidance implies a higher full-year figure than July's $107.5B, and 2027 consensus is about $114B.

questions_for_management.question: What underwriting changes are you making as you tighten credit, and which sectors drive the criticized-exposure increase? Does the card NCO guide of 3.2% still hold given a rising unemployment risk?

why.text: Management is tightening terms, and the card guide implies an H2 rate near 3.0%.

questions_for_management.question: How large is your direct and indirect exposure to AI and hyperscaler financing, and what single-name limits apply as the Security and Resiliency Initiative scales past $230B?

why.text: Management flagged concentration as a focus while financing AI and security-related projects.
